mainTopic: What a thief owes for a stolen animal, and when a partial sale or flawed slaughter exempts him from ארבעה וחמשה
overview: The amud opens with the last words of the previous discussion, which tie רבא's rule about an animal's father to the view of רבי שמעון. Then רבא asks what a thief owes if he steals a bull that was set aside for a general vow of an עולה. רבא answers his own question: the thief only owes the smallest valid עולה, a sheep according to the רבנן or a bird according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. A new משנה lists cases where a thief pays only כפל and not ארבעה וחמשה, such as selling all but a small part of the animal or slaughtering it improperly. The גמרא asks which held-back part counts. רב and לוי disagree, and the גמרא traces four different views among the תנאים to different readings of וּטְבָחוֹ וּמְכָרוֹ. Next, a ברייתא about partners who steal raises a contradiction, which רב נחמן finally resolves by asking whether one partner slaughtered with the other's consent. רבי ירמיה and רב פפא then ask about other kinds of holding back, such as keeping the fetus or cutting off a limb before the sale, and these questions end in תיקו. The amud closes with a new ברייתא about a thief who has someone else slaughter or sell the animal for him, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Closing the previous discussion: a case of a non-cloven father
steps.stepSummary: The last words of the earlier sugya give the case where רבא's rule about the father makes a difference. The mother was made pregnant by an animal without split hooves, and this follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference shows up where the mother was made pregnant by a non-cloven animal, according to רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the discussion from the previous page. It names the exact case where רבא's rule about the father's role actually changes the הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rule is only useful if there is a case where it matters. Here the case is a mother that became pregnant from a קלוט, an animal born to kosher parents but without split hooves. רבי שמעון holds that such an animal is not kosher, so a baby it fathers is affected through its father.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose hooves are not split, even though its parents were kosher
Became pregnant

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not the start of a new topic. It is the tail end of the discussion on the previous page, and the new topic begins with בעי רבא.

phrases.english: where it became pregnant from a non-cloven animal,
phrases.notes: A non-cloven animal here means one born to kosher parents that came out without split hooves.

phrases.english: in accordance with Rabbi Shimon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer from the previous page by naming the case where the rule matters.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule matters when the mother was impregnated by a קלוט, according to רבי שמעון.

steps.title: רבא asks: what must a thief repay for a stolen bull vowed as a burnt-offering?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether a thief who stole a bull set aside for an עולה may pay back a sheep according to the רבנן, or a bird according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: Someone said, "I take upon myself to bring an עולה." He set aside a bull, and someone else came and stole it. Can the thief free himself by paying a sheep, according to the רבנן, or a bird עולה, according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a brand-new question. He asks whether the thief must replace the bull itself, or only the cheapest offering that would still fulfill the owner's vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner's vow only required "an עולה." He chose a bull on his own, even though a smaller animal would have been enough. So the question is whether the thief owes what was actually taken, a bull, or only what the owner truly needs to fulfill his vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a question he was unsure about
"It is upon me to bring an עולה": a general vow to bring a burnt-offering
Set aside an animal for a specific offering
Frees himself from what he owes
A burnt-offering made with a bird

phrases.english: Rava asked:
"It is upon me to bring a burnt-offering,"
and he set aside a bull,
and another person came and stole it;

phrases.aramaic: מִי פָּטַר גַּנָּב נַפְשֵׁיהּ בְּכֶבֶשׂ – לְרַבָּנַן,
phrases.english: can the thief exempt himself with a sheep, according to the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: בְּעוֹלַת הָעוֹף – לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה?
phrases.english: or with a bird burnt-offering, according to Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the previous discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a thief may repay the minimum offering that fulfills the vow, instead of the bull he actually stole.

steps.title: The משנה behind the two opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. According to the רבנן, a person who vows an עולה brings a sheep. According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, he may even bring a turtledove or a young pigeon.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone says "It is upon me to bring an עולה," he brings a sheep. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: he may bring a turtledove or a young pigeon.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to show where the two opinions in רבא's question come from. It quotes the משנה that sets the smallest offering allowed for a general vow of an עולה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that a general vow of an עולה means an animal, so the smallest acceptable one is a sheep. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds that even a bird counts as an עולה. That is why רבא's question gives two possible minimum payments.

keyTerms.meaning: A sheep, the smallest animal offering
Turtledove
Young pigeon

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishnah:
"It is upon me to bring a burnt-offering": he must bring a sheep.
phrases.notes: A bull is also fine; a sheep is simply the smallest animal that counts.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
He may bring a turtledove or a young pigeon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the two opinions mentioned in רבא's question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a general vow of an עולה, the רבנן require at least a sheep, while רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allows even a bird.

steps.title: The two sides: just the title of a burnt-offering, or the best way to do the מצוה?
steps.stepSummary: רבא lays out his doubt. Perhaps the owner only took on the general title of an עולה, so any valid עולה is enough. Or perhaps the owner can tell the thief that he wants to do the מצוה in the best way, with a bull.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the law? Do we say that he only took on himself the title "עולה"? Or perhaps the owner can say to the thief, "I want to do the מצוה in the best possible way"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why the question is hard by giving the reasoning for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: the owner's real obligation is only "an עולה," so replacing it with any valid עולה leaves him with no loss. Side two: the owner had chosen to do the מצוה in its finest form, a bull. The thief took that chance away from him, so he should have to restore it.

keyTerms.meaning: The title or status of an עולה, without a specific animal in mind
He took upon himself
Or perhaps: introduces the other side of a doubt
Doing a מצוה in the best, finest way

phrases.english: What is the law?
Do we say:
he took upon himself the title of a burnt-offering;
or perhaps, the owner can say to the thief:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא מִצְוָה מִן הַמּוּבְחָר בָּעֵינָא לְמֶיעְבַּד?
phrases.english: "I want to perform the מצוה in the choicest way"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to רבא's question and lays out the reasoning on each side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the owner's loss is measured by his basic obligation or by his choice to do the מצוה in the best way.

steps.title: רבא answers his own question: the minimum offering is enough
steps.stepSummary: After asking the question, רבא answers it himself. The thief may repay a sheep according to the רבנן, or a bird according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he asked the question, רבא went back and answered it: The thief frees himself with a sheep according to the רבנן, and with a bird עולה according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers his own question. The thief only has to give the smallest offering that fulfills the owner's vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא picks the first side: the owner only took on the title of an עולה. His wish to do the מצוה in the best way does not make the thief owe a bull. The minimum still changes with each opinion in the משנה: a sheep for the רבנן, a bird for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

keyTerms.meaning: After he had asked the question
He went back and answered it himself
Thief

steps.whatToRemember: For an animal set aside for a general vow of an עולה, a thief only owes the smallest valid עולה. That is a sheep for the רבנן and a bird for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. The owner's wish for מצוה מן המובחר does not change what the thief owes.

phrases.english: After he raised the question, he went back and resolved it:
the thief exempts himself with a sheep according to the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: בְּעוֹלַת הָעוֹף לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: and with a bird burnt-offering according to Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in steps 2 and 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The thief may repay the smallest valid עולה: a sheep for the רבנן, a bird for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: What the owner took on is the title of an עולה, so the thief only owes the smallest offering that fulfills it.

steps.title: רבא's ruling taught as a plain statement
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא teaches רבא's ruling directly, without the question. The thief may repay a sheep according to the רבנן, or a bird according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רב איקא taught this as a plain ruling. רבא said: if someone said 'I take on an עולה' and set aside a bull for it, and someone else stole the bull, the thief can free himself by giving a sheep according to the רבנן, or a bird עולה according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבא's teaching. In this version there is no question at all, only the final ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבא asked a question and then answered it himself. רב אחא בריה דרב איקא skips the question and states the answer as a plain rule. The outcome is the same: the thief only has to replace the smallest valid עולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Teaches it openly, as a plain statement and not as a question
'I take upon myself an עולה,' a general vow to bring a burnt-offering
Set aside an animal for a קרבן
Frees himself from what he owes
An עולה brought from a bird

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions agree on the ruling. The thief only has to give the owner the minimum valid עולה: a sheep according to the רבנן, or a bird according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika
teaches it explicitly:
phrases.notes: He gives רבא's ruling straight out, without the back-and-forth question we just saw.

phrases.english: Rava said:
if one said 'It is upon me to bring a burnt-offering' and set aside a bull,
and another person came and stole it,
he exempts himself with a sheep, according to the Rabbis,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְעוֹלַת הָעוֹף לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה.
phrases.english: and with a bird burnt-offering, according to Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּהֶדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different way of teaching רבא's ruling from Steps 2-5, stated as a ruling instead of a question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thief of a bull set aside for a general עולה vow may repay a sheep according to the רבנן, or a bird according to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: New משנה: cases that pay only double, not four or five
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists cases where a thief pays כפל but not ארבעה וחמשה. These are partial sale, partnership, invalid slaughter, ripping, and tearing out the pipes.
steps.simpleTranslation: A thief pays double but not four or five times in these cases: he sold the animal except for one hundredth of it, he was a partner in the animal, he slaughtered it and it became נבלה in his hands, he ripped it open, or he tore out its pipes.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists cases where a thief who stole an ox or sheep pays only the double payment and not the extra fourfold or fivefold fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fourfold and fivefold fine applies only when the thief fully sells or properly slaughters the animal. Each case here is missing one of those things. The sale is not complete, the animal was partly his, or the slaughter was not a valid שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Partnership, shared ownership
Became a נבלה, meat that is not kosher because of bad slaughter
One who stabs or rips the animal instead of slaughtering it
One who tears out the windpipe or gullet while slaughtering
The double payment a thief pays
The four or five times payment for slaughtering or selling a stolen sheep or ox

steps.confusionAlert: The thief is not let off completely. He still pays כפל. He only avoids the extra ארבעה וחמשה fine.

phrases.english: Mishnah:
If he sold it except for one hundredth of it,
or he had a partnership in it;
one who slaughters and it became non-kosher in his hand,
one who rips it, and one who tears out the pipes,
pays the double payment,
but does not pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ מְכָרוֹ חוּץ מֵאֶחָד מִמֵּאָה שֶׁבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the earlier discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partial sale, partnership, or invalid slaughter means the thief pays כפל only, not ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: What counts as 'one hundredth'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what part of the animal the משנה means when it says 'except for one hundredth of it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'except for one hundredth of it' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking what kind of part the thief must hold back so that the sale is not counted as a full sale. This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not say whether any small piece is enough or only a certain kind of part. The גמרא wants to know exactly which part the thief must keep.

keyTerms.meaning: What? It is used to ask for the meaning of a phrase

phrases.english: Gemara:
What is 'except for one hundredth of it'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the first case in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which part of the animal the thief must keep for the sale to count as only partial.

steps.title: רב: a part permitted through slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רב says the part held back must be something that becomes permitted to eat through the animal's שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: it means except for something that becomes permitted together with the animal through slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. Only a part that becomes permitted through שחיטה counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, holding back the horns or fleece is not enough. Those parts can be used even without שחיטה. The kept part must be one that depends on the slaughter, like meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes permitted through שחיטה

phrases.english: Rav said:
except for something that becomes permitted with it through slaughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חוּץ מִדָּבָר הַנִּיתָּר עִמּוֹ בִּשְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The kept part must be one that becomes permitted through שחיטה.

steps.title: לוי: even the fleece, with a supporting ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: לוי says keeping even the fleece is enough, and a ברייתא teaches the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי said: even except for its fleece. And a ברייתא also teaches: except for its fleece.
steps.whatsHappening: לוי gives a different answer. Keeping back even the fleece makes the sale partial, and the גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: לוי allows a wider range of parts than רב, since fleece does not need שחיטה. The words 'וכן תניא' show that a ברייתא agrees with לוי, which makes his view stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: Its fleece, the wool shearings
And so it is taught, introducing a ברייתא that supports a view
A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה

phrases.english: And Levi said: except for its fleece.
And so it is taught in a baraita:
except for its fleece.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to Step 8 that disagrees with רב and is backed by a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even keeping back the fleece makes the sale partial.

steps.title: A baraita challenges רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא against רב. It says that holding back a leg, horn, or fleece exempts the thief, and רבי gives the standard of a part that holds back the slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: An objection was raised: if he sold it except for its foreleg, its hind leg, its horn, or its fleece, he does not pay four or five. רבי says: if he held back something that holds back the slaughter, he does not pay four or five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's view with a ברייתא. The ברייתא keeps going in the next step, and step 13 spells out why it is a problem for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא says horn or fleece is enough. Those parts do not become permitted through שחיטה, so this goes against רב. רבי gives a different standard: a part connected to the slaughter itself.

keyTerms.meaning: Something that holds back or affects the slaughter

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
If he sold it except for its foreleg, except for its hind leg,
except for its horn, except for its fleece,
he does not pay the fourfold or fivefold payment.
Rabbi says: if it is something that holds back the slaughter,
he does not pay the fourfold or fivefold payment,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's answer from Step 9 using a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule that the kept part must become permitted through שחיטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא exempts a thief who held back the horn or fleece. Those parts do not become permitted through שחיטה, so this goes against רב.

steps.title: The challenging teaching finishes with two more opinions
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי says that if the part held back does not hold back the שחיטה, the thief still pays four and five. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says holding back the horn exempts him, but holding back the fleece does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the part he kept is something that does not hold back the slaughter, he pays four and five. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: if he sold it except for its horn, he does not pay four and five. If he sold it except for its fleece, he does pay four and five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the ברייתא it brought against רב, finishing רבי's rule and adding a third opinion. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא spells out why this is a problem for רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now three views in this ברייתא. The תנא קמא says a leg, horn, or fleece exempts the thief. רבי says only a part that holds back the שחיטה exempts him. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says the horn exempts him but the fleece does not. None of these say what רב said, which is that it depends on whether the part becomes permitted to eat through the שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds back the slaughter: a part the שחיטה depends on
Its horn
Its fleece (its wool)

phrases.english: And [if he kept a part] that does not hold back the slaughter —
phrases.notes: This is still רבי talking, finishing the rule from the last step. He means a part whose absence would not stop the שחיטה from working.

phrases.english: he pays the four and five payment.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
[If he sold it] except for its horn —
he does not pay the four and five payment;
except for its fleece —
he does pay the four and five payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא begun in step 11 as a challenge to רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's rule (step 9) that the part held back must become permitted to eat through the שחיטה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All three opinions in the ברייתא use a different standard than רב's, so רב seems to have no תנא behind him.

steps.title: לוי has a source, but whom does רב follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the problem plainly: לוי follows the תנא קמא of the ברייתא, but רב matches none of its opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for לוי, because he holds like the first תנא. But רב, whom does he follow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now says outright why the ברייתא is a problem: לוי has support, but רב does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said even the fleece exempts the thief, which is exactly what לוי said in step 10. רב's standard, a part made permitted to eat through the שחיטה, is not the same as the תנא קמא's, רבי's, or רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's in this ברייתא. So the question is whether רב has any תנא at all.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (for one side)
The first, unnamed opinion in a teaching
Like whom? Which opinion does he follow?

phrases.english: Granted, according to Levi — [he holds] like the first tanna;
but according to Rav — like whom [does he hold]?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְלֵוִי כְּתַנָּא קַמָּא אֶלָּא לְרַב כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ברייתא quoted in steps 11–12 into a clear challenge against רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A view held by an אמורא should match some תנא. In this ברייתא, לוי matches one, but רב matches none.

steps.title: רב follows a different teaching of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that רב follows another ברייתא. There, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says keeping a foreleg or hind leg exempts the thief, but keeping the horn or fleece does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: רב holds like this תנא, as it was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says, if he sold it except for its foreleg or except for its hind leg, he does not pay four and five. If he sold it except for its horn or except for its fleece, he does pay four and five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by finding a different ברייתא that agrees with רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this ברייתא the leg exempts the thief, and a leg is meat that becomes permitted to eat through the שחיטה. The horn and fleece do not exempt him, because the שחיטה does not make them permitted. That is exactly רב's standard, so רב does have a תנא behind him.

keyTerms.meaning: Like this תנא
Its foreleg (literally, its hand)
Its hind leg

steps.whatToRemember: לוי follows the תנא קמא of the first ברייתא, where even fleece exempts the thief. רב follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר in the second ברייתא: a leg exempts him, but horn and fleece do not, because only meat becomes permitted through the שחיטה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר gives different rulings in the two ברייתות. In the first, keeping the horn exempts the thief. In the second, it does not. The גמרא simply picks the second version as רב's source.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that both אמוראים have a תנא behind them, so their argument is a real disagreement about what counts as holding back part of the sale.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי: רַב דְּאָמַר – כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא,
phrases.english: They say: Rav said [his view] in accordance with this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: as it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
phrases.notes: This is a different ברייתא from the one in steps 11–12, even though it has the same speaker.

phrases.english: If he sold it except for its foreleg or except for its hind leg —
he does not pay the four and five payment.
Except for its horn, except for its fleece —
he does pay the four and five payment.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי רַב דְּאָמַר כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13 by finding a תנא who agrees with רב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding an alternate תנאי source that supports the challenged אמורא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's view seemed to have no support from any תנא, since the ברייתא had only other standards.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows the second ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: a leg (permitted through שחיטה) exempts the thief, but horn and fleece do not.

steps.title: What is the root of the disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what idea lies behind the different opinions in the ברייתות.
steps.simpleTranslation: On what point do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks what reasoning stands behind each of the four opinions we just saw.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 11-14 listed four opinions about which held-back part exempts the thief from paying four and five. Now the גמרא wants the reason behind each one, which it will give one by one in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: On what point do they disagree?

phrases.english: On what point do they disagree?
phrases.notes: "They" means all four opinions from the two ברייתות in the last few steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that רב has a source (Step 14), the גמרא goes back and explains the reasoning of all the opinions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind each opinion about which held-back part counts as a שיור.

steps.title: The first opinion: the whole animal must be slaughtered or sold
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא learns from the פסוק that the thief must slaughter or sell all of the animal to pay four and five.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds: "and slaughters it" means we need all of it, and "or sells it" means we need all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the תנא קמא. He reads the words "וּטְבָחוֹ" and "וּמְכָרוֹ" as meaning the whole animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the פסוק says "it," the תנא קמא understands it to mean all of the animal. So if the thief holds back anything at all, even the fleece, it is not the whole animal, and he does not pay four and five.

keyTerms.meaning: "And slaughters it", a word from the פסוק about the thief
"Or sells it", a word from the same פסוק
We need all of it

phrases.english: The first tanna holds:
"And slaughters it": we require all of it,
"Or sells it": we require all of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question of Step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא reads "it" as the entire animal, so any held-back part exempts the thief.

steps.title: רבי: only parts affected by slaughter count
steps.stepSummary: רבי reads "and slaughters it" as covering only parts affected by שחיטה, and selling is compared to slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי holds: "and slaughters it" means things that are affected by slaughter, which leaves out things not affected by slaughter. "Or sells it" is like slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי. He says the פסוק only cares about the parts of the animal that שחיטה affects.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Horns and fleece are not changed by שחיטה, so holding them back does not count, and the thief still pays four and five. Since "וּמְכָרוֹ" comes right next to "וּטְבָחוֹ", the same rule applies to selling.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughter
To leave out (to exclude)
Similar to, like

phrases.english: And Rabbi holds:
"And slaughters it": something that is affected by slaughter,
to exclude something that is not affected by slaughter;
"Or sells it": similar to slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second opinion's reasoning, which disagrees with the תנא קמא's reading of the same words.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי counts only parts affected by שחיטה, and applies the same rule to selling.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: horn counts, fleece does not
steps.stepSummary: In the first version, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says a horn is a real שיור because it is not meant to be cut off, but fleece is not, since it is meant to be sheared.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds: a horn, which is not meant to be cut off, is a holding back, and he does not pay four and five. Its fleece, which is meant to be sheared, is not a holding back, and he pays four and five.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first version of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. His test is whether the part normally stays on the living animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A horn stays on the animal, so keeping it means the thief truly kept part of the animal, and he is exempt. Fleece is normally sheared off anyway, so keeping it does not count, and he must pay four and five.

keyTerms.meaning: Horn
Meant to be cut off or sheared
A part held back by the thief
Its fleece (wool)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds:

phrases.aramaic: קַרְנָא, דְּלָא לְמִגַּז קָיְימָא – הָוֵי שִׁיּוּר,
phrases.english: A horn, which is not meant to be cut off, is a holding back,
and he does not pay the four and five payment;

phrases.aramaic: גִּיזּוֹתֶיהָ, דִּלְמִיגַּז קָיְימִי – לָא הָוֵי שִׁיּוּר,
phrases.english: its fleece, which is meant to be sheared, is not a holding back,
and he pays the four and five payment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the third opinion's reasoning, using a new test: is the part meant to be cut off?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A part not meant to be cut off (horn) is a שיור; a part meant to be cut off (fleece) is not.

steps.title: The other version of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר: only legs count
steps.stepSummary: The other teaching from רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's school says legs count as a שיור because they need שחיטה to be used, but horns and fleece do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other תנא of the school of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds: its forelegs and hind legs, which need slaughter, are a holding back, and he does not pay four and five. Its horns and fleece, which do not need slaughter, are not a holding back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second version of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, the one רב follows (Step 14). His test is whether the part needs שחיטה before it can be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Legs are only eaten after שחיטה, so they belong to the slaughtered animal, and keeping one exempts the thief. Horns and fleece can be used without שחיטה, so keeping them does not count. This explains רב's position.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other tanna
Of the school of
Its forelegs and hind legs
Need slaughter (to be used)

steps.whatToRemember: Four tests for a שיור: the תנא קמא says anything counts; רבי says only parts affected by שחיטה; רבי שמעון בן אלעזר (first version) says only parts not meant to be cut off, like the horn; the other version (רב's source) says only parts that need שחיטה, like the legs.
steps.confusionAlert: The two versions of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר disagree about the horn. In the first version, keeping the horn exempts the thief. In the second version, it does not.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִידַּךְ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר:
phrases.english: And the other tanna of the school of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar holds:
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא brought in Step 14 to support רב.

phrases.aramaic: יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו, דִּצְרִיכִי טְבִיחָה – הָוֵי שִׁיּוּר,
phrases.english: Its forelegs and hind legs, which need slaughter, are a holding back,
and he does not pay the four and five payments;

phrases.aramaic: קַרְנֶיהָ וְגִיזּוֹתֶיהָ, דְּלָא צְרִיכִי טְבִיחָה – לָא הָוֵי שִׁיּוּר.
phrases.english: its horns and its fleece, which do not need slaughter, are not a holding back.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ תַּנָּא דְּבֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the fourth and last reasoning, using yet another test: does the part need שחיטה to be used?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Parts that need שחיטה to be used (legs) are a שיור; horns and fleece, which do not, are not.

steps.title: The two reports of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר clash
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the two teachings in the name of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: one teaching of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר contradicts another teaching of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the two teachings of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר from Steps 18 and 19 do not match. It raises this as a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, a horn counts as a real leftover (שיור), but in the second version, a horn does not count, and only legs do. One person cannot hold both views, so something needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty or contradiction
A part of the animal left over that the thief did not slaughter or sell

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: the teaching of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar
phrases.notes: This points back to the two versions in Steps 18 and 19: horn counts versus horn doesn't count.

phrases.english: contradicts the teaching of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar!

steps.triggerLanguage: קַשְׁיָא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אַדְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two reports of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר given in Steps 18 and 19
steps.kashyaTarget: The two reports of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One version says a horn is a שיור and the other says it is not, so the same תנא seems to contradict himself

steps.title: Two teachers reported his view differently
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that two different תנאים passed down רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view in two different ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are two תנאים, and they disagree about what רבי שמעון בן אלעזר held.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר did not say two opposite things. Two later teachers reported his opinion differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The clash is moved off of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר himself and placed on the people who quoted him. Each report stays valid as one תנא's version of his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Two תנאים (teachers of the ברייתא period)
According to, or about the view of

phrases.english: There are two Tannaim,
and they disagree about the view of Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי תַּנָּאֵי וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Two different reporters of the same תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר himself held two opposite views
steps.terutzMaskana: Each version comes from a different תנא reporting his view, so he did not contradict himself
steps.whatToRemember: When one תנא seems to contradict himself, the גמרא can answer that two later teachers reported his view differently.

steps.title: A ברייתא on damaged animals and partners
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that stealing a damaged animal, or an animal owned by partners, makes the thief liable, but partners who steal are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: Someone who steals an animal missing a limb, a lame animal, or a blind animal is liable. So is someone who steals an animal owned by partners. But partners who steal are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about who pays ארבעה וחמשה. It sets up a contradiction that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal's damage does not lower the thief's liability, and an animal owned by several people still counts as a full theft. But when the thieves themselves are partners, the ברייתא exempts them.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal missing a limb
A lame animal
A blind animal
Partners

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who steals an animal missing a limb,
or a lame one, or a blind one,
and likewise one who steals an animal of partners, is liable.
phrases.notes: Liable here means paying four or five times, after he slaughters or sells the animal.

phrases.english: But partners who stole are exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about ארבעה וחמשה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A damaged animal or an animal owned by partners brings ארבעה וחמשה, but partners who steal are exempt

steps.title: Another ברייתא says partners who steal are liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a different ברייתא that says partners who steal are liable, which contradicts the first one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But another ברייתא teaches: Partners who stole are liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last line of the ברייתא. It brings another ברייתא that says the opposite about partners who steal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said partners who steal are פטור, and this one says they are חייב. Both cannot be true as stated, so the גמרא needs a way to fit them together.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt / liable

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Partners who stole are liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the last clause of the ברייתא in Step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that partners who stole are exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא rules the exact opposite: partners who stole are liable

steps.title: רב נחמן splits the two cases
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says the ברייתות speak about different cases: a partner stealing from his own partner, and partners stealing together from an outsider.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: There is no difficulty. Here, it is talking about a partner who stole from his fellow partner. There, it is talking about a partner who stole from the outside world.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the contradiction. Each ברייתא is talking about a different kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exempt ruling is about one partner stealing an animal he partly owns from his partner. The liable ruling is about partners who team up to steal from an outsider. So each thief is fully guilty there.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (the cases are different)
From his fellow partner
From the outside world, from a stranger

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said: It is not difficult;
here, it is a partner who stole from his fellow partner,
phrases.notes: This is the case where they are exempt. He partly owns the animal he took.

phrases.english: there, it is a partner who stole from the outside world.
phrases.notes: This is the liable case: partners who teamed up to steal someone else's animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction in Step 23
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות speak about the same case of partners who steal
steps.terutzMaskana: Exempt means a partner stealing from his partner; liable means partners stealing together from an outsider
steps.confusionAlert: "Partners who stole" can mean two different things here. It can mean stealing an animal that they themselves share, or teaming up to steal someone else's animal. רב נחמן's answer depends on keeping these apart.

steps.title: רבא objects from a ברייתא on "and slaughters it"
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב נחמן with a ברייתא that exempts both a partner stealing from his partner and partners who steal, since the פסוק requires slaughtering all of the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged רב נחמן: You might think that a partner who stole from his fellow partner, and partners who stole, should be liable. That is why the פסוק says "and slaughters it": we need all of it, and here that is missing!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב נחמן's answer. He brings a ברייתא that exempts partners who steal together too, not only a partner stealing from his own partner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said partners who steal together from an outsider are liable. But this ברייתא lists them as exempt, next to the partner who stole from his partner. Its reason is that "וּטְבָחוֹ" requires the thief to slaughter the whole animal on his own, and the one who slaughters has not done that.

keyTerms.meaning: One might think (opens a possibility the ברייתא will reject)
The פסוק teaches us
"And slaughters it" — the word in the פסוק that requires the whole animal

phrases.english: Rava challenged Rav Nachman:
One might think that a partner who stole from his fellow partner,
and partners who stole, should be liable;
the verse teaches: "And slaughters it"
we need all of it, and that is missing!
phrases.notes: Each thief owns part of the animal, or shares it with fellow thieves. So he didn't slaughter a whole animal that belongs to someone else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's answer from Step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that partners who steal together from an outsider are liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא exempts partners who stole, in addition to a partner who stole from his partner, because "וּטְבָחוֹ" requires the whole animal. That contradicts רב נחמן's ruling that they are liable.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the partners' exemption to the same rule from earlier in the sugya: "וּטְבָחוֹ" means all of the animal.

steps.title: רב נחמן's new answer: slaughtering with or without the partner's knowledge
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן now says both ברייתות are about partners who stole together. If one partner slaughtered with the other's consent, they are liable. If he slaughtered without the other's consent, they are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב נחמן said: There is no contradiction. One ברייתא is about a partner who slaughtered with his fellow partner's knowledge. The other is about a partner who slaughtered without his fellow partner's knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא's challenge knocked out רב נחמן's first answer, so רב נחמן gives a brand-new way to explain the contradiction between the two ברייתות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first answer split the cases by who was robbed: the partner himself, or an outsider. Now both ברייתות are about partners who stole together from someone else, and the only difference is consent. With consent, the one who slaughters acts for both partners, so the whole animal was slaughtered and they are liable. Without consent, he only slaughtered for himself, so they are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: Partner
Slaughtered
With his fellow's knowledge and consent
Without his fellow's knowledge

steps.whatToRemember: Final answer for partners: if one slaughters with the other's consent, they are liable. If he slaughters without consent, they are exempt.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא;
phrases.english: Rather, Rav Nachman said: it is not difficult;
here, it is about a partner who slaughtered with his fellow's knowledge,

phrases.aramaic: כָּאן בְּשׁוּתָּף שֶׁטָּבַח שֶׁלֹּא לְדַעַת חֲבֵירוֹ.
phrases.english: there, it is about a partner who slaughtered without his fellow's knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer from step 24, which רבא knocked down in step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): the same kind of theft, but slaughtered with or without consent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות differ based on who was robbed: the partner or an outsider.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both ברייתות are about partners robbing an outsider. Consent to the slaughter decides liability.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה asks about selling a stolen animal while holding something back
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks about a thief who sold the stolen animal but kept back thirty days of use, its work, or its fetus. Does that count as holding back part of the animal?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: If the thief sold the animal except for thirty days, or except for its work, or except for its fetus, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי ירמיה asks whether these kinds of holding back count as not selling the whole animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A thief only pays four or five times the animal's value if he sold the whole animal. Keeping part of it back (שיור) exempts him. רבי ירמיה wants to know whether keeping back time, work, or a fetus counts as that kind of holding back.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked, raised a question he was unsure about
He sold it (the animal)
Except for
Its work
Its fetus

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
if he sold it except for thirty days;
phrases.notes: He means the thief keeps the right to use the animal for thirty days before the buyer gets it.

phrases.english: except for its work;
except for its fetus; what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: holding back part of a sale (שיור).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does keeping back thirty days of use, the animal's work, or its fetus count as holding back part of the animal and exempt the thief?

steps.title: Narrowing the fetus question to one opinion
steps.stepSummary: If a fetus is part of its mother, keeping it back is clearly holding back part of the animal. The question only exists if a fetus is a separate being: does being attached make it count, or does the fact that it will separate make it not count?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says a fetus is like its mother's thigh, there is no question, because he clearly held back part of the animal. The question is according to the one who says a fetus is not its mother's thigh. Do we say that since it is attached to the mother, it counts as holding back? Or perhaps, since it is going to separate from her, it does not count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly where the fetus question applies and what the two sides are.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known argument about whether a fetus is part of its mother's body. If it is part of her, keeping it is like keeping a piece of her. If it is a separate being, we must decide which matters more: that it is attached to her right now, or that it is going to separate later.

keyTerms.meaning: A fetus is like its mother's thigh, meaning a part of her body
Holding back part of what is sold
Attached
To separate

steps.confusionAlert: "Thigh" here is not literal. It just means the fetus counts as one of the mother's body parts.

phrases.english: According to the one who says
a fetus is its mother's thigh,

phrases.aramaic: לָא תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ, דְּהָא שַׁיַּיר בַּהּ;
phrases.english: do not ask, for he clearly left over part of it;

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ – אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר
phrases.english: when you should ask, it is according to the one who says
that a fetus is not its mother's thigh; what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: מֵימָר אָמְרִינַן: כֵּיוָן דִּמְחוּבָּר בַּהּ – הָוֵי שִׁיּוּר;
phrases.english: Do we say: since it is attached to her, it counts as holding back;

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, כֵּיוָן דִּלְמִפְרַשׁ מִינַּהּ קָאֵי,
phrases.english: or perhaps, since it is going to separate from her,
it does not count as holding back?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר עוּבָּר יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא לָא תִּבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and narrows the third case of רבי ירמיה's question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: If a fetus is a separate being, does its present attachment to the mother make keeping it a שיור, or does the fact that it will separate cancel that?

steps.title: Another way to frame the fetus question
steps.stepSummary: Others frame it differently. Since a fetus is not part of its mother, maybe keeping it is not holding back. Or maybe it is, because the fetus becomes permitted to eat only through the mother's slaughter, which ties it to her body.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: Since the fetus is not its mother's thigh, it does not count as holding back. Or perhaps, since it needs to become permitted together with her through her slaughter, it is like holding back part of her body?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of how the fetus question was asked, with a different reason on the "it counts" side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the reason it might count is that the fetus is physically attached. In this version, the reason is a halachic link: a fetus becomes permitted when its mother is slaughtered (שחיטה). That link might make keeping the fetus like keeping part of the mother's body.

keyTerms.meaning: To become permitted
Kosher slaughter

phrases.english: There are those who say:

phrases.aramaic: כֵּיוָן דְּלָאו יֶרֶךְ אִמּוֹ הוּא – לָא הָוֵי שִׁיּוּר;
phrases.english: since it is not its mother's thigh, it does not count as holding back;
or perhaps, since it needs
to become permitted together with her through slaughter,
it is like one who left over part of her body?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the question from step 28.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the fetus's need to become permitted through its mother's slaughter make keeping it a שיור, even though it is not part of her body?

steps.title: The questions stay unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: רבי ירמיה's questions are left without an answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes רבי ירמיה's questions without deciding them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source is found to settle whether keeping back thirty days, work, or a fetus counts as holding back part of the animal. So the questions remain open.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand; the question stays unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה's questions about holding back time, work, or a fetus when selling a stolen animal are left open (תיקו).

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the questions from steps 27 through 29.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The questions are unresolved: we do not know whether these kinds of holding back exempt the thief.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about a thief who cut off a limb and then sold the animal
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks: a thief stole an animal, cut off one of its limbs, and then sold it. Does he pay ארבעה וחמשה?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: If someone stole an animal, cut off a part of it, and then sold it, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא brings a new case to add to the earlier questions about holding back part of the animal. Here the thief cut a limb off before he sold the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that if a thief holds back part of the animal when he sells it, he does not pay ארבעה וחמשה. In רב פפא's case the limb was cut off before the sale, so the buyer gets the whole of what is left. The question is whether this still counts as holding back part of the animal.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (an open question)
He cut it off (cut off a limb of the animal)
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If he stole it, cut off part of it, and sold it, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "It" is the stolen animal. The question is whether he pays four or five times its value.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another unanswered question to רבי ירמיה's questions about a thief who holds back part of the animal.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does cutting off a limb before selling count as holding back part of the animal, so that the thief is exempt from ארבעה וחמשה?

steps.title: The two sides of רב פפא's question
steps.stepSummary: Side one: he did not sell everything he stole, so he is exempt. Side two: he held back nothing from what he did sell, so he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say: part of what he stole, he did not sell? Or maybe: from what he did sell, he did not hold anything back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets out the two possible ways to look at רב פפא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we measure from the theft, the thief did not sell the whole animal he stole, so it is like holding back part of it and he is exempt. If we measure from the sale, the buyer received everything that was sold and nothing was held back from it, so he is liable. The whole question is which moment we look at: the stealing or the selling.

keyTerms.meaning: Do we say...? (opens the first side of a question)
Or perhaps... (opens the second side)
He sold
He held back, kept something for himself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with רבי ירמיה's case. There the thief held back something as part of the sale itself, like work or a fetus. Here the limb was already cut off before the sale, so the sale itself held nothing back.

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן: מַאי דִּגְנַב – הָא לָא זַבֵּין;
phrases.english: Do we say: what he stole, he did not sell?

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא, מָה דְּזַבֵּין – הָא לָא שַׁיַּיר?
phrases.english: Or perhaps: from what he sold, he did not hold anything back?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן: מַאי דִּגְנַב הָא לָא זַבֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two ways of looking at the question asked in step 31.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do we measure from what was stolen, which makes him exempt, or from what was sold, which makes him liable?

steps.title: רב פפא's question is left unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends רב פפא's question with תיקו, meaning there is no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves רב פפא's question without an answer, just as it did with רבי ירמיה's questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source settles whether we look at the stealing or the selling. So the case of a thief who cuts off a limb and then sells the animal stays undecided.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand: the question remains unanswered

steps.whatToRemember: This whole series of questions about holding back part of the animal ends in תיקו. That includes the questions about work, a fetus, and a cut-off limb.

phrases.english: Let it stand unanswered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes רב פפא's question the same way step 30 closed רבי ירמיה's questions.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no answer on whether cutting off a limb before the sale exempts the thief from ארבעה וחמשה.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a thief who has someone else slaughter or sell the animal
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא begins with cases where a thief gives the stolen animal to another person, who slaughters it or sells it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If he stole and gave it to someone else, who slaughtered it; if he stole and gave it to someone else, who sold it;
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא. It is setting up the cases now, and the ruling comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the thief himself did the slaughtering or selling. This ברייתא asks what happens when another person does it for him, acting as his שליח. The ברייתא's ruling continues past this point.

keyTerms.meaning: He gave it to another person
He slaughtered
He sold

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If he stole, and gave it to another, who slaughtered it;
phrases.notes: The other person slaughtered it for the thief, on his behalf.

phrases.english: if he stole, and gave it to another, who sold it;

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: גָּנַב, וְנָתַן לְאַחֵר וְטָבַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the run of unanswered questions: slaughtering or selling done by someone else for the thief.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא lists cases where another person slaughters or sells the stolen animal for the thief. Its ruling continues past this point.
